title: H168: Add sentiment surprise (relative to 8-quarter baseline) design note + PEAD.txt academic anchor
rationale: PEAD.txt (JFQA 2022, Meursault et al.) shows SUE.txt from transcripts earns 3.9bp daily alpha vs 2.6bp for price-based SUE — 50% stronger. QuantPedia BLMECT research finds 'sentiment surprise' (current sentiment minus 8-quarter rolling mean) achieves Sharpe 0.76, CAR 5.89% — outperforming absolute sentiment level. Both suggest H168 should use RELATIVE sentiment (delta from historical baseline) rather than raw FinBERT scores. Design implication: compute finbert_score_surprise = score_t - mean(score_{t-1:t-8q}) for each stock, then filter on positive surprise. H168 v2 should test both absolute score and surprise-relative variants. Tertile sorting (top/bottom 33%) beats quintile/decile splitting.
content:
### PEAD.txt — Text-Based Earnings Surprise (JFQA 2022)

Meursault, Liang, Routledge & Scanlon (2022, *JFQA*) construct SUE.txt from earnings call transcripts — a text-based earnings surprise measure. Key results (2010–2019 sample):
- SUE.txt spread portfolio earns **3.9bp daily alpha** vs 2.6bp for traditional price-based SUE (+50% stronger)
- 1-SD increase in text surprise → 3–6% of SD increase in 63-day CAR
- Text signal and price signal are complementary — combining both > either alone

This is the academic anchor for H168. It confirms that earnings call TRANSCRIPT language carries more predictive information than the gap-up price action alone.

**QuantPedia BLMECT design parameters** (highest-performing NLP-PEAD variant, 2025):
- **Sentiment surprise** = current_sentiment − mean(last 4 quarters) — stronger than absolute level
- Tercile sorting (top/bottom 33%) outperforms quintiles/deciles
- 4-quarter baseline lookback optimal
- 4-week holding period
- Universe: 500 most liquid stocks, price > $5

H168 v2 should test: `finbert_surprise = weighted_score_t − mean(weighted_score_{t-4q..t-1q})`
